summary: Stellantis talks on Brampton end with no deal but more talks, Trump calls Canada "emboldened", and Halifax hosts a big security forum this weekend.
body: Friday's meeting between Stellantis, federal Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, Premier Doug Ford and Unifor ended without a decision on the Brampton plant, which Stellantis plans to sell to defence firm Roshel. Ford called it "challenging" but "productive" and said Ottawa should ease the roughly $1 billion a year Stellantis pays in emissions costs.[^1] Joly said Stellantis can keep the plant and work with Ottawa, or face legal action for "hundreds of millions of dollars" under its 2022 funding deal; the company has 30 days to respond to a default notice.[^1]

On trade, Trump said on Friday that Canada is feeling "emboldened" but that he wants a "fair" deal, and that he will be ready to talk when Canada's trade deficit with the US reaches zero.[^2] Carney said this week that a good deal is possible, but "if the U.S. doesn't want to do a deal, we're busy."[^2] The government says his Asia trip concluded free-trade talks with ASEAN and the Philippines and extended a tariff-relief arrangement with China to December 2028.[^3]

This weekend the Halifax International Security Forum brings defence leaders from more than 70 countries to Nova Scotia, with Ukraine and shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz high on the agenda. No members of the Trump administration are attending, CTV reports.[^4]
differences: On Brampton, Ford says Ottawa should cut emissions costs to keep the plant viable, while Joly says Stellantis must keep its promises or repay public money.[^1] On trade, Trump says Canada must close its deficit with the US first; Carney says Canada is building other partnerships.[^2]

reads.title: Stellantis meeting 'challenging' but 'productive', Premier Ford says
reads.summary: What each side said after Friday's Brampton meeting, the $529 million funding deal at stake, and how the plant ended up idle.
